name: May 2021 Leverage Cascade (Tesla U-turn + China bans, May 19 crash day)
speed: BTC ~-30% intraday on May 19 (≈$43k -> $30,001 in roughly 12h, bulk in ~6h); ETH -47% intraday; -54% (BTC) / -56% (ETH) from ATHs in 5 weeks / 1 week respectively; ~$8-9B liquidations and >60% of futures OI destroyed within days
summary: 19 мая 2021: BTC −30% внутри дня ($43k→$30k), ETH −47%, $8-9B ликвидаций за сутки, >60% открытого интереса уничтожено. Пеги держали ВСЕ стейблы. Контрольный сценарий «чистый рыночный крах»: NAV стейбл-книги цел, но операционная среда (газ, ставки, ликвидность) штормит 48 часов, а форвардный APY падает на месяцы. Книга SPA на 2026-08: aave_v3 40% / pendle (PT_USDC) 20% / maple 15% / morpho_steakhouse 15% / кэш USDC 10%.

timeline.event: Context: BTC prints cycle ATH ~$64,800-64,900 (venue-dependent); aggregate BTC futures open interest peaks at $27.4B mid-April (Glassnode) — the leverage that later unwinds

Elon Musk announces Tesla suspends BTC vehicle payments over coal/energy concerns (~6pm ET). BTC drops ~5% within minutes from ~$54.8k and ~17% over the following day; ETH had printed its ATH ($4,330-4,384 depending on feed) earlier the same day
BTC slides to lowest since early March (~$46-49k); Musk's ambiguous tweets May 16-17 about Tesla possibly selling its BTC keep pressure on; BTC grinds to ~$42-45k by May 18

Three Chinese industry bodies (NIFA, China Banking Assoc., Payment & Clearing Assoc.) issue joint statement barring financial and payment institutions from any crypto-related services (trading, clearing, settlement, savings/trust/pledging)
Sell-off accelerates through the European morning: BTC breaks $40k from ~$43k as spot selling (retail-driven per Chainalysis) meets long liquidations; time approximate

Cascade climax (~9am ET, time approximate): BTC prints $30,001.51 (Coin Metrics via CNBC), lowest since late January, ~-30% intraday and ~-54% from April ATH; ETH prints $1,902.08 (CoinDesk data via Forbes), >56% below its week-old ATH; some feeds show BTC wicks to ~$29,563-30,066

Exchange infrastructure buckles: Binance disables ETH/ERC-20 withdrawals citing network congestion (~1h) and suspends leveraged-token trading; Coinbase/Coinbase Pro report intermittent downtime and delayed ETH/ERC-20 withdrawals; Kraken, Gemini, WazirX, CoinDCX degraded. Later research (Baumgartner & Guettler; IWH) documents Binance halting retail trading and its futures dislocating ~7x wider vs other venues

On-chain gas war: Ethereum gas oscillates 1,500-1,700 gwei for ~an hour with peaks >2,000 gwei (Delphi Digital) as liquidators/arbitrageurs and margin traders race; average ERC-20 transfer >$140, average Uniswap swap $411-457

Partial V-recovery within hours: BTC rebounds from ~$30k toward $38-40k; ETH, down 47% intraday at the low, finishes the session ~-28% (Deribit). Funding rates on perps flip from persistently positive to negative — shorts paying longs

24h derivatives wipe: >$8B liquidations across ~800,000 traders per bybt (some aggregations put it at ~$9.0B; Bybit CEO estimated $8-10B; true figure higher since Binance throttled its liquidation feed from late April 2021). Record DeFi liquidation day: $377M collateral liquidated across Aave/Compound/Maker; Maker settles $41M debt via 177 auctions with only ~$12k of losses; DAI trades $0.996-1.015 — no depeg, no meaningful bad debt
Relief rally: ETH +~14%, BTC back above $40k intraday; stablecoins trade at slight premium as flight-to-stables continues

Second China shock: State Council Financial Stability Committee chaired by Vice Premier Liu He vows to 'crack down on bitcoin mining and trading behavior' — first explicit State Council targeting of mining. BTC slides >6% on the headline and the bounce dies

Second leg down into the weekend: BTC hits ~$31,100-32,000 (venue-dependent Sunday low), ~-52% from ATH; week closes ~$34,700, worst week (-25.4%) since March 2020 (FXEmpire feed). ETH retests ~$2,100-2,200
BTC reclaims $40,000 (AFP); acute phase over. Aggregate futures OI ends the episode >60% below the $27.4B April peak (Glassnode) — the leverage reset that defines the event
Aftermath (outside window): China mining ban escalation drives BTC briefly below $30k ($28.8k area); range $29-42k persists until late July; new ATHs only in Oct-Nov 2021

btc.window: 2021-05-12 high (~$56.7-58k, feed-dependent) -> 2021-05-19T~13:00Z low ($30,001.51 Coin Metrics; $29,563-30,066 wicks on some feeds)
btc.notes: may19_close and may23_low are venue-dependent approximations (~$36.7-38.8k close; $31.1-32k Sunday low); week ending May 23 was -25.4% (FXEmpire feed)

eth.notes: biggest one-day ETH loss to date: -47% intraday, closed ~-28% (Deribit Insights)

total_crypto_market_cap.notes: roughly $1T lost market-wide over the crash period and >$500B off BTC's peak market value (CNBC/Fortune); exact peak/trough caps not pinned to a single source — use CoinGecko/CMC series to replay

btc_futures_open_interest.notes: >60% of the $27.4B mid-April aggregate OI cleared by end of the sell-off (Glassnode). A conflicting '$42B->$25B' claim in a Phemex retrospective was discarded as inconsistent with contemporaneous data

stablecoins.notes: Held peg; traded at slight premium amid flight to stables; served as exit liquidity (Glassnode). Venue-level wicks existed but no sustained deviation.
Held peg; mild premium. May 2021 is a NON-depeg stress scenario for USDC-based portfolios.
Oscillated $0.996-1.015 (Cointelegraph, May 24 2021); Maker liquidations worked; supply contracted as vaults were closed/liquidated.

defi_impact.tvl: Aggregate DeFi TVL fell roughly 40% from its ~May 11-12 peak to the May 23-24 trough (DeFiLlama total TVL series replays this precisely; ETH-denominated TVL fell ~30% from highs per later TechCrunch/DeFiLlama retrospective). Exact USD endpoints not pinned by a contemporaneous source — take from DeFiLlama API.
defi_impact.liquidations_defi: Record single day: $377M collateral liquidated across Aave+Compound+Maker on May 19 (Cointelegraph Consulting/Dune); May 2021 total >$1.17B. 1,168 addresses liquidated on Aave, 714 on Compound; MakerDAO liquidated 2,255 vault positions in May.
defi_impact.liquidations_cex: $8-9B futures liquidations in 24h (~800k traders, bybt); undercounted because Binance capped its public liquidation feed from late April 2021.
defi_impact.bad_debt_notes: Maker Liquidations 2.0 (deployed weeks earlier) settled $41M of debt via 177 Dutch auctions, earned $5.1M in fees, and incurred only ~$12k of losses across 2 auctions (Messari) — no material bad debt anywhere in blue-chip DeFi; sharp contrast to Black Thursday 2020.
defi_impact.gas: Peak >2,000 gwei; 1,500-1,700 gwei sustained ~1 hour (Delphi Digital); average ERC-20 transfer >$140, average Uniswap swap $411-457; $1,000+ fee transactions reported stuck.
defi_impact.oracles: No major oracle failure reported on Chainlink/Maker OSM (unlike March 2020) — liquidations executed against live prices; however Binance halted its own market/transaction data feed during the worst window, blinding strategies keyed to it (IWH/SSRN studies).
defi_impact.withdrawal_freezes: CEX-side only: Binance ETH/ERC-20 withdrawals disabled (~1h) and leveraged-token trading suspended; Coinbase delayed ETH/ERC-20 withdrawals with intermittent platform downtime; no DeFi protocol froze withdrawals; no protocol paused or became insolvent.
defi_impact.dex_liquidity: DEXs absorbed record flow: Uniswap v3 record ~$2.6B daily volume May 19; May 2021 on pace for record ~$140B monthly DEX volume (Messari). Slippage/exit costs dominated by gas, not AMM depth, for majors and stables.
defi_impact.stablecoins: USDT/USDC held peg on major venues (slight premiums — flight to stables); DAI oscillated $0.996-1.015 on May 19; only small algorithmic stables suffered.
defi_impact.chains_bridges: Ethereum L1 remained live but congested; no bridge or chain outage central to the event (BSC congested; its lending forks saw heavy liquidations — e.g. Venus VAI/XVS distress days later).

causes.primary: Unwind of record perpetual-futures leverage built up into the April 2021 top ($27.4B BTC OI), triggered by back-to-back sentiment/regulatory shocks: Tesla suspending BTC payments (May 12) and China's industry-body ban on institutional crypto services (May 18), climaxing in a self-reinforcing long-liquidation cascade on May 19.
secondary: Retail-dominated spot selling into weak depth (Chainalysis: selling driven by retail, not institutions)

Exchange outages/degradation (Coinbase intermittent downtime, Binance retail-trading and data-feed halt, ETH/ERC-20 withdrawal freezes) removed bid-side liquidity and amplified panic; Binance futures dislocated ~7x vs other venues (Baumgartner & Guettler, SSRN 4260876)
Ethereum congestion (>2,000 gwei) slowed on-chain deleveraging and made position defense expensive
China State Council (Liu He) mining/trading crackdown statement May 21 killed the rebound and forced the May 23 retest
Musk 'Tesla may sell' innuendo May 16-17 kept sentiment bleeding between the two shocks
causes.mechanism: Leverage builds Jan-Apr (OI $27.4B, funding persistently positive) -> Tesla U-turn May 12 breaks momentum, BTC -17% over the week -> China industry-body ban May 18 adds regulatory fear -> May 19: spot selling pushes BTC through $40k, triggering margin calls; forced selling of longs feeds back into price (~$8-9B liquidated / ~800k traders in 24h, ~50% BTC pairs) -> exchanges degrade under load, retail cannot add margin or buy the dip, order books thin -> BTC -30% intraday to $30,001, ETH -47% -> on-chain: collateral values crash, record $377M DeFi liquidations execute in gas wars at 1,500-2,000+ gwei -> shorts/sellers exhaust, funding flips negative, V-bounce to $38-40k -> May 21 State Council statement re-ignites selling -> May 23 retest ~$31k -> OI >60% cleared, market enters 2-month $29-42k range.

contagion: Tesla BTC-payment suspension (May 12) -> momentum break, -17% week
China industry-body service ban (May 18) -> regulatory fear premium
Spot selling breaks $40k (May 19) -> perp long margin calls -> $8-9B liquidation cascade, ~50% in BTC pairs
Liquidation flow -> exchange overload: Coinbase/Binance degraded, Binance ETH/ERC-20 withdrawals frozen -> buyers locked out, books thin -> deeper wick to $30k
Collateral crash -> record on-chain deleveraging: $377M Aave/Compound/Maker liquidations -> gas war >2,000 gwei -> exits cost $140-457 per tx
Panic rotation to stables -> stablecoin premiums (no depeg; DAI 0.996-1.015)
Seller exhaustion -> funding flips negative -> V-bounce to $38-40k
China State Council mining/trading crackdown (May 21) -> second leg -> May 23 low ~$31k -> miner capitulation phase into June (June 22 sub-$30k)

recovery.recovered: partially within hours/days; fully by Q4 2021
recovery.time_to_recover: Bounce to $38-40k same day (+~30% off low); $40k reclaimed May 26 (7 days); but the leverage reset held BTC in a $29-42k range ~2.5 months (deeper low $28.8k on June 22 during China mining-ban escalation); prior ATH not exceeded until ~Oct 20 2021 (BTC ~$67k) and ETH ~Nov 2021 ($4,878) — ~5-6 months
recovery.notes: Classic post-cascade pattern: violent intraday V (short-covering into negative funding), failed relief rally killed by the next headline (May 21 State Council), retest of lows (May 23), then long sideways accumulation with funding neutral-to-negative before recovery. For a yield portfolio the more durable effect was the collapse of leverage demand: stablecoin lending/perp-basis yields fell from double digits pre-crash to low single digits for months.

confidence_notes: Solid (multi-source): May 19 BTC low $30,001.51 (Coin Metrics via CNBC; Fortune 'nearly $30,000'; CoinDesk 'below $31k' on its BPI); ETH low $1,902.08 (CoinDesk data via Forbes); >$8B 24h liquidations (bybt via CoinDesk) with honest range $8-9B (some aggregations $9.01B) and Bybit CEO's $8-10B estimate — bybt undercounts because Binance throttled its liquidation feed from late April 2021; gas >2,000 gwei peak / 1,500-1,700 sustained (Delphi via FXStreet); $377M DeFi liquidations May 19 (Cointelegraph Consulting); Maker $41M/177 auctions/$12k losses (Messari); DAI 0.996-1.015 and centralized stables holding peg (Cointelegraph); OI: >60% of $27.4B mid-April peak cleared (Glassnode) — a conflicting '$42B->$25B' figure from a Phemex retrospective was discarded as inconsistent. Contested/approximate: all intraday TIMES (the ~13:00 UTC trough is inferred from CNBC's ~9am ET reporting — verify against 1m klines); May 12 pre-crash reference high ($56.7-58k feed-dependent) and ETH ATH ($4,330.75 CMC vs ~$4,384 other feeds); May 19 close (~$36.7-38.8k) and May 23 Sunday low (~$31.1-32k) are venue-dependent — I report ranges; FXEmpire's feed shows a $29,563 weekly low, below Coin Metrics' $30,001; total market-cap loss (~$1T market-wide, >$500B BTC) is order-of-magnitude press framing, not a precise series — set null and replay from CoinGecko; DeFi TVL drawdown (~-40% USD) is inferred from DeFiLlama-shaped retrospectives, not a contemporaneous number — pull exact endpoints from the DeFiLlama API; funding 'flipped negative' is directionally multi-source but I have no free archival print of the exact May 19 funding values (replayable via Binance funding-rate API). Musk tweet time 22:06 UTC May 12 is approximate (evening ET). Inference vs fact: the causal mechanism (leverage cascade amplified by exchange outages) is the consensus reading, supported by the SSRN/IWH microstructure studies, but 'outages deepened the wick' is analytical inference, not a measured counterfactual.

data_availability.price_series: FREE and high quality. Binance public data archive (data.binance.vision) has full 1m klines CSVs for BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT etc. covering May 2021 — best replay source. Coinbase Exchange REST /candles gives 1m for BTC-USD/ETH-USD (rate-limited pulls). Bitstamp OHLC API free. CoinGecko free tier: only DAILY granularity that far back. Note venue divergence on May 19 (Binance futures dislocated) — replay should use at least 2 venues.
data_availability.stablecoin_prices: FREE: Binance 1m klines for USDC/USDT, BUSD/USDT pairs (data.binance.vision); Kraken OHLC for USDT/USD, DAI/USD; on-chain Curve 3pool swap prices via Dune (free tier) or BigQuery public Ethereum dataset. CoinGecko daily for sanity check. DAI $0.996-1.015 range is press-sourced and replayable on-chain.
data_availability.tvl: FREE: DeFiLlama API (api.llama.fi) — historical daily total TVL and per-protocol (aave, compound, makerdao) covers May 2021; use it for exact peak/trough since contemporaneous articles don't pin USD endpoints.
data_availability.liquidations_cex: NOT freely obtainable at granularity. Coinglass (ex-bybt) historical liquidation series is paywalled; Binance capped its liquidation websocket feed from late April 2021 so even paid aggregates undercount May 19. Headline $8-9B exists only as press snapshots.
data_availability.liquidations_defi: FREE: fully replayable on-chain — Aave v2 LiquidationCall, Compound LiquidateBorrow, Maker Clipper auction events via Dune free tier / BigQuery public dataset / TheGraph.
data_availability.gas: FREE: Etherscan daily average gas price chart CSV (free download); intraday percentiles via BigQuery public bigquery-public-data.crypto_ethereum (free quota). Pre-EIP-1559, so use gas_price on transactions, not base fee.
data_availability.funding_rates: FREE: Binance futures API /fapi/v1/fundingRate returns full history incl. May 2021 (8h prints); Bybit/OKX partial history free. Confirms the negative flip post-May 19.
data_availability.open_interest: NOT freely obtainable for 2021: Binance OI endpoint only serves ~30 days; Coinglass/Glassnode historical OI paywalled; The Block chart page shows the series but no free API export. Rely on Glassnode's published '$27.4B peak, >60% cleared' figure.
data_availability.exchange_outage_record: FREE: status.coinbase.com history, Binance/Coinbase tweets, and the SSRN/IWH papers for the Binance microstructure record.

spa_relevance.headline: The best 'pure market crash, pegs hold' control scenario: a $100k USDC yield portfolio survives with NAV ~intact, but every operational assumption about exits gets stressed for ~48h and forward APY collapses for months.

positions.aave_v3_usdc_supply: Hit channels: (1) brief utilization/borrow-rate spike during the cascade, then a months-long APY collapse as >60% of futures OI (the leverage demand behind stable borrow rates) is destroyed — post-May stable supply APYs fell from ~8-15% to ~2-4%; (2) protocol solvency held (May-2021-analog liquidation engines produced only ~$12k losses on $41M at Maker; Aave/Compound cleared $300M+ without bad debt), so principal channel is quiet; (3) same-day exit costs 10-100x normal gas ($140+ per transfer, $400+ per swap at 2,000 gwei).
positions.pendle_pt: Pendle did not exist yet (mainnet June 2021) — map by analogy: implied yields gap UP in the panic then collapse after; PT mark-to-market whipsaws and AMM exit liquidity thins exactly when you'd want to sell; hold-to-maturity PT on a solvent underlying loses nothing to this event, but any NAV marked off PT spot prices shows a drawdown the portfolio can't realize away.
positions.maple: Maple had just launched (May 2021, ~$0 scale). Analog channel: its borrowers are market makers — a -30% day with $8-9B liquidations is exactly when MM credit stress peaks; termed loans mean lender USDC is NOT withdrawable on demand. Unpriced if the system assumes always-withdrawable.
positions.morpho_steakhouse_usdc: Analog channel: underlying lending-market utilization spikes as borrowers scramble -> withdrawal liquidity can be partially unavailable for hours-days; APY spikes then collapses with the leverage reset; curator/oracle risk quiet in this event.
positions.cash_10pct: Unimpaired; its real value here is avoiding forced on-chain transactions during the 2,000-gwei window.

unpriced_if_usdc_equals_1_and_always_wit: Gas/exit-cost shock: rebalancing or de-risking during the cascade costs 30-100bps of a $100k portfolio per round trip (this event's binding constraint, not the peg)
Utilization-driven withdrawal delay on lending markets/vaults (hours-days) — not a freeze but violates 'instantly withdrawable'

APY regime collapse: the dominant realized P&L effect for a yield portfolio — forward stablecoin yields fell ~60-80% for months after the deleveraging; a backtest assuming pre-crash APYs persist overstates income badly
CEX/off-ramp outage risk: Coinbase/Binance degradation + ETH/ERC-20 withdrawal freezes block the CEX leg of any exit route for ~hours
Data-feed outage: Binance halted market data mid-crash — any monitor keyed to a single feed goes blind exactly at the trough (argues for SPA's quorum/fail-CLOSED design)
What this scenario does NOT test: USDC depeg, protocol insolvency, DeFi withdrawal freezes, oracle failure — pair with H03 (Black Thursday) and the UST/USDC-depeg scenarios for those
spa_relevance.kill_switch_note: A crypto-beta portfolio hits HARD_KILL (-10%) within hours on May 19; the SPA stable-yield portfolio would see near-zero NAV drawdown (pegs held, no bad debt) — this event instead stresses SENSE-layer (feed outages), exit-cost modeling, and APY-forecast honesty.

assumptions: Протоколы книги (кроме Aave) не существовали в мае 2021 — каналы-аналоги: спайк→коллапс ставок и 3%-дисконт PT (implied-yield spike, WARN-уровень).
Пеги держали (историч. факт) — потерь капитала нет.
